explanation: Newton later said that watching an apple fall in his family's garden set him thinking about gravity. No early account says it hit him on the head.

claims.text: Isaac Newton's Principia, published in 1687, set out his laws of motion and his law of universal gravitation.
Galileo died in 1642 and Kepler in 1630, and Einstein was born in 1879, so none of them wrote the 1687 Principia.
Newton told friends that watching an apple fall in the garden of his family home set him thinking about gravity.
No early account says that the apple hit Newton on the head.
